description: Every bump merges itself once its PR is green and the release has aged; the packageRules below are the exceptions. The repo-wide defaults carry the policy so that a shape nobody has named yet (a new manager, a new depType, a new file) merges under the same terms as everything else instead of waiting for a person by accident, which is how transitive pins, CalVer packages and action inputs each spent weeks as a 'manual' row before anyone noticed there was no decision behind it. The condition that makes the default safe is enforced outside this file: a dependency may only be added together with a PR-time run that exercises it (AGENTS.md 'Adding a dependency'), and ci.yml's suite-size job fails a bump that passes by shrinking what CI checks. Three-day age because a compromised or broken upstream release is usually pulled or yanked within days of going public, and hash-locked installs do not help with that (they pin whatever release was current). Renovate merges by itself after its own stability check; platformAutomerge is false so that GitHub's native auto-merge, which lands a PR as soon as the required ci-ok passes and knows nothing of renovate/stability-days, can never route around the age. Labels: nothing by default, `manual-merge` only where a rule below says a person decides, `age-gated` on the digests digest-age-gate.yml merges, `security` added on advisory PRs; so an open Renovate PR with no label is green-and-waiting or red, never forgotten. docs/CI.md 'Dependency updates' is the human-readable table of the same policy; change both together.

logLevelRemap.matchMessage: /^pip-compile: dependency not found in lock file$/

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Open a security PR the moment an advisory lands instead of waiting for the weekly schedule. osvVulnerabilityAlerts covers the uv/pip-compile *.lock files that GitHub's native Dependabot does not parse. Renovate applies this block as a `force` package rule appended AFTER the packageRules below (workers/repository/init/vulnerability.ts), carrying its own defaults for the alert: minimumReleaseAge null, schedule [], prCreation immediate, groupName null. So a security PR is ungrouped, opens at once and skips every age below, the seven-day one on majors included; whether it then merges itself is decided by the same rules as any other update, and since the default is automerge and the only row a person decides is a pyyaml major, a security PR waits for a human only when it is that, or red. Transitive pins: the pip-compile manager extracts every lock entry pyproject.toml does not declare with depType `indirect` and `enabled: false`, and this force block is what enables one, so a transitive dependency moves only in a security PR (and in the weekly lock maintenance, which refreshes every pin). `addLabels` (not `labels`) so `security` stacks on whatever the rules below left. This is the continuous-detection half of the pip-audit split (PR audit informational, publish audit blocking — see .github/workflows/ci.yml). Verified against Renovate 44.175.

pip-compile.description: The 16 'dependency not found in lock file' warnings, all against requirements-build.lock, are EXPECTED. Do not restructure the locks — or revert the lock-header style — to silence them. They date from #333 (2026-06-09), which rewrote the uv headers to the parseable long form (--extra=X, --output-file=Y): before that Renovate threw a header-parse error and this manager tracked nothing at all, so the warnings are the visible cost of pip-compile coverage actually working. #472 (2026-08-07) took the count 15 -> 16 by adding mkdocs-material. They surface on the Dependency Dashboard as a single deduped 'Repository Problems' bullet (workers/repository/common.ts keys the set on level+message, so all 16 collapse into one), and only on runs where extraction is not served from the repo cache (cache key = base-branch SHA + config hash + manager fingerprints) — so the section appeared and disappeared between runs rather than being permanent. The logLevelRemap entry at the top of this file now demotes that exact message to debug so it never reaches the dashboard (verified 16 -> 0 warnings with dep extraction byte-identical). This suppresses nothing that worked: because the problem set dedupes on level+message, a genuine 17th occurrence was ALREADY invisible — it collapsed into the same single bullet as the 16 expected ones. The message still appears under LOG_LEVEL=debug. Note the remap matches on message text only (getRemappedLevel receives just the string), so it cannot be scoped to requirements-build.lock; a real missing-lock-dep elsewhere is also demoted, and in practice surfaces instead as a CI failure when something imports the absent dep. Cause: Renovate parses --extra out of each lock header into compileArgs.extra (manager/pip-compile/common.ts) but the dep-matching loop (manager/pip-compile/extract.ts) never consults it — it compares every pep621 dep in pyproject.toml against one lock and warns for each one absent, with no notion that --extra was meant to narrow the set. A guard in that same loop means only the FIRST lock referencing pyproject.toml runs the comparison, and that is alphabetically-first requirements-build.lock, whose --extra=container set is our narrowest (build, plus the PyYAML runtime dep) — so the noise is worst-case by accident of filename ordering. The 16 are: requires-python and hatchling (build-system.requires, which can never appear in a pip lock), the intentional compose-lint[lint] self-reference, and optional-dependency pins that legitimately live in requirements-dev.lock / requirements-docs.lock / requirements.lock (including the corpus/matplotlib group deliberately absent from every lock). Update coverage is NOT affected: verified 2026-08-08 with `npx renovate@latest --platform=local --dry-run=extract` that each warned dep is still extracted with its currentValue and datasource=pypi and no skipReason, so bumps still open normally; only lockedVersion, a display field, goes unset. No upstream issue tracked this as of 2026-08-08; the fix would be for that loop to skip deps whose managerData.depGroup falls outside compileArgs.extra (pep621 already tags them) and to skip the requires-python / build-system.requires depTypes.

poetry.description: pyproject.toml is already covered by pep621 + pip-compile. The poetry manager detects the same [project] deps but is not in the python group rule, so it spawned duplicate ungrouped PRs that bumped pyproject without regenerating the lockfiles (e.g. renovate/ruff-0.x, #329).

customManagers.description: The Docker Compose plugin the differential suites are graded against. The runner image pins its own — images/ubuntu/toolsets/toolset-2404.json in actions/runner-images holds it at 2.38.2 while docker/compose is on 5.x — and that version is not a choice this project made: CI was grading ADR-036's include: orderings, every one measured on Compose 5.5.0, against a binary that refuses the documents describing them ('services.web conflicts with imported resource'). .github/scripts/install-compose-plugin.sh installs the pin ahead of the image's copy; this manager moves it. Its bumps merge under the repo defaults: ci.yml is in the `code` change filter, so the bump PR runs the differential suites it exists to re-prove, and a green run means the new binary still agrees with every graded ordering. A red run is precisely the PR that has to be triaged into 'Compose changed', 'we were wrong', or 'a new deliberate divergence', and Renovate never merges a red PR, so that triage still reaches a human.

Release binaries that ci.yml jobs download from a GitHub Release and verify against the release's checksums file (actionlint, hadolint). The version is a bare X.Y.Z literal beside a `# renovate:` annotation; the tag carries a v prefix, so extractVersion strips it. Their bumps merge under the repo defaults: each runs the linter it bumps on the PR itself (ci.yml is in the `workflows` change filter for actionlint and in the `dockerfile` filter for hadolint), so a green run is the review and a red one waits for a human with the tool's release notes.

Container images the premise validator runs (busybox, and python:3.13-alpine for the checks busybox cannot express). They are string constants in a Python script, which no built-in manager reads, so until this manager existed both digests sat where they were pinned (busybox from May 2026, python from June) with nothing to say they were stale. Each pin is a `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=…` line, then `NAME = (`, then one string `"name:tag@sha256:<index digest>"`; the tag is what Renovate looks the digest up by. Digest refreshes and tag moves alike merge under the repo defaults, because the rule-premises job re-runs every premise against the new image on the PR, and busybox's error wordings are asserted there verbatim, so a release line whose wordings changed goes red.

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions: SHA-pin every uses: with version comment (CLAUDE.md).

Workflows that run only after the tag is pushed (publish.yml and the reusable workflows it calls) get their own group, because Renovate automerges a group only when every update in it is eligible, and this group's two publish-only actions wait seven days (the rule below) while the rest wait three: in one group a fresh attest-build-provenance minor would hold the weekly actions batch for four extra days.

Python runtime + dev deps batched into one PR. pip-compile tracks the uv-generated requirements*.lock files: their .lock extension is matched by no pip-family manager by default, leaving transitive pins (e.g. urllib3) invisible to Renovate and weekly lockFileMaintenance a no-op for these files.
Docker base images: digest-pin per CLAUDE.md.

Production runtime + build-stage base images bypass the weekly schedule. Debian and distroless rebuilds carry CVE patches we cannot apply ourselves (no shell, no apt at runtime), so opening the bump PR same-day shrinks the window between upstream patch and our published image. debian then merges under the defaults; distroless is age-gated (its rule below).

Majors wait seven days instead of three. The PR-time review is the same as for a minor (the full suite, the smokes, and ci.yml's suite-size job, which fails a bump that passes by collecting fewer tests), so a green major proves what a green minor proves. The extra days are for a different reason: a major's first week is when early adopters find its regressions and the x.0.1 lands, so waiting usually means the PR proposes the version people actually run, and CI exercises that one. Applies to every manager: dev tooling, actions on either path, the ubuntu runner image (datasource github-runners, which carries release dates), the release binaries ci.yml downloads, and a container image's tag moving to a new release line (debian:14, postgres:19). pyyaml majors are the one exception, next rule.

A pyyaml major is a person's call, not a bump. pyproject.toml declares the range `pyyaml>=6.0.2,<7` for every user of the wheel, so a major crosses that ceiling and changes what pip resolves for them, which after 1.0 is a compose-lint MAJOR with its own release decision (docs/compatibility.md). A pyyaml minor moves only the hash-pinned locks, never the wheel's range, and merges under the defaults.

Minors of the two release actions that cannot run without publishing wait seven days. actions/attest-build-provenance writes attestations to GitHub's API and pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish uploads to an index, so there is no PR-time run of either that does not publish; the other three release-only actions (gh-action-sigstore-python, sbom-action, cosign-installer) do run on the PR, in ci.yml's release-actions-smoke job, and merge under the defaults. What a human review of these two could catch, a bad minor, fails the release run before anything irreversible (verify-tag, build and the TestPyPI smoke precede the release-gate approval) and is recovered by re-running the job or with a patch release. What it could not catch, a compromised release of the action, is what the SHA pin and the age are for; seven days because here the age is the only review.

Digests from gcr.io and ghcr.io (distroless, the oss-fuzz builder, vhs) cannot be aged by Renovate: its docker datasource takes releaseTimestamp from Docker Hub's tag_last_pushed and from nowhere else, and under the default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-required a digest with no timestamp is pending forever and never even opens a PR. So the age is lifted here and automerge is off, and .github/workflows/digest-age-gate.yml merges each one once it has aged 72h by gcr.io's registry-stamped upload time, or by the head commit's age where the registry gives none (first-seen is never earlier than publish). When upstream rebuilds faster than that and Renovate keeps moving the PR to a digest that has not aged, the gate opens its own catch-up PR (head age-gate/<image>, same label) for the newest digest the PR has already pinned that has aged, so the pin trails upstream by at most about three days instead of waiting for a quiet week (#1152). The review on the PR is the same as for a Docker Hub digest: dockerfile-digests fails a per-arch pin and docker-smoke builds and runs the image on amd64 and arm64, both required via ci-ok. `age-gated` is the label the gate selects on: rename both or neither. The gate adds `manual-merge` to one it refuses for a reason other than age (red, conflict, draft, fork, hand-touched). Goes away if upstream Renovate ships a registry-agnostic release timestamp (renovatebot/renovate#39064). Verified against 44.132 (lookup/digest.ts, datasource/docker releaseTimestampNote).

Demo toolchain: the compose-lint pin in scripts/demo records which release the committed GIF was rendered on, so it moves only as part of a deliberate demo regeneration (docs/RELEASING.md), never via Renovate. pillow/numpy and transitives in the same lock stay managed; ci.yml's demo-lock job installs that lock on the PR.

Forgejo smoke harness: NOT Renovate's. The hosted runner cannot look up codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo or data.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner (Dependency Dashboard: 'no-result' + 'Error obtaining docker token', while a local `renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup` resolves both — the hosted runner's egress, not the registries), so the same-day bump rule that replaced #748's tests/ move never produced a PR, and a Renovate PR could not pass anyway: forgejo-smoke asserts docs/forgejo.md's 'Verified on Forgejo X, runner Y' line against the live stack, and Renovate cannot move that line. forgejo-smoke-bump.yml owns both files instead (daily; scripts/forgejo_smoke_bump.py). Disabled here so two writers never race on the same pin; the file stays listed on the dashboard for visibility.

Workaround for renovatebot/renovate#45236 (fix in flight: renovatebot/renovate#46645), scoped to the update types it affects. Renovate checks minimumReleaseAge twice. The lookup stage has the real data: it ages a digest/pinDigest against the newest release matching the current value and, under the default internalChecksFilter=strict, holds the branch back (Dependency Dashboard 'Pending Status Checks') until the age passes; pin and lockFileMaintenance are exempt there by design because they introduce no new release. The branch stage then re-checks from upgrade.releaseTimestamp, which only version updates carry, and under the default timestamp-required marks every one of these update types yellow forever: renovate/stability-days never clears and automerge silently never fires. #933 (lockFileMaintenance, 2026-09-28) sat pending until a human merged it; #786 and #709 had automerged cleanly before the behaviour changed upstream. timestamp-optional here lets the branch stage stand aside for exactly the upgrades it has no data for. It does not shorten any wait: the three-day gate on digests is still enforced at lookup for every image that has a timestamp (Docker Hub), and the images without one have the age lifted and automerge off in the age-gated rule above. Remove once the upstream fix ships. Verified against 44.132 (workers/repository/update/branch/index.ts stability block vs lookup/digest.ts).
